# dsh-taskboard-epic

Epic panel for **DeepSeek Harness**. It stacks the `[总任务]` (epic) cards of a
dsh-taskboard project i

n their `epic:children` order and lets the order of the
module arcs be rearranged by drag or by butt

eir `epic:children` order and lets the order of the
module arcs be rearranged by drag or by buttons.

The panel is client-only: it reads the taskboard's public same-origin API
(`/dsh-taskboard/state`, `

/dsh-taskboard/tasks/:id/update`) and renders into the
`sidebar.panellist` and `main` slots. There i

s no host-side state and no new
route, so the host half of this package intentionally does nothing.
## What it does

- Groups the cards of one epic into a stack, ordered by `epic:children`.
- Shows each module's posit

ion, code, name and version on the arc.
- Reorders the arc by dragging a module or by using the move

buttons; the new
order is written back to the taskboard through its public update API.
- Marks the

start module, the middle modules and the end module of the arc, so
the dependency shape of a project
is visible at a glance.
## Requirements

- `dsh-taskboard` (the taskboard plugin) must be installed; the panel renders
data that the taskboar

d exposes.
- A browser client (the panel is a web-client plugin).

## Notes

- The panel writes only through the taskboard's own update endpoint; it never
edits project data dir

ectly.
- Card ordering is stored on the epic card itself, so the order survives a
restart and is sha
red by everyone looking at the same project.
## English summary

`dsh-taskboard-epic` is a client-side panel for DeepSeek Harness. It stacks the
epic cards of a dsh-

taskboard project in their `epic:children` order, shows each
module's position, code, name and versi

on along the arc, and marks the start,
middle and end modules. The order can be changed by drag or b

y buttons, and the
new order is written back through the taskboard's public update API, so it
persis
ts and is shared across everyone viewing the project.
